column1: # SKIP CENSUS MANIFEST — the tests that are allowed to skip, and what they need.
# GATE-INTEGRITY-20260819 section 10. `nv27b_twin_parity` prints "SKIP: ckpt/twin absent" and
# PASSES, and round 2 gave it a caller (.github/workflows/ci.yml), so CI reports it green in
# perpetuity on every executor without checkpoints. The count of such tests is now a NUMBER this
# repo states out loud rather than a property nobody measures.
# Columns: crate <TAB> test path (as libtest prints it) <TAB> file:line <TAB> the SKIP message
# exactly as written in the source (format placeholders included — tools/skip-census.py matches
# the literal prefix at run time and the full string against the source).
# tools/skip-census.py verify compares this file with a static scan of the crate in BOTH
# directions. An undeclared skipping test FAILS (it would otherwise be born invisible); a stale
# row FAILS (it inflates the budget and silently permits a different skip). A moved line number
# is a NOTE, not a failure.
# tools/skip-census.py run compares the number that ACTUALLY skipped against a named budget,
# default 0. Where the budgets live and why:
#   tools/local-ci.sh           gguf budget 10, rig-side with artifacts present (rehomed
#                                        2026-09-02 from tools/validate-h100.sh, deleted with
#                                        the Hopper lane). Measured 2026-09-02: 212 passed,
#                                        10 skipped (ckpt/twin, Hy3-repack, iq3s artifacts not
#                                        staged). local-ci's kernel-check additionally enforces
#                                        11 skipped cells against MEMRA_CI_KC_SKIP_BUDGET.
#   .github/workflows/ci.yml budget 12 — a hosted runner has no /data at all, so all twelve
#                                        skip. Twelve is therefore the count of model-backed
#                                        assertions CI is blind to, stated rather than hidden.
#                                        If it grows, CI reds and someone looks.
#   tools/portable-suites.sh    budget 0 for memra-tier, memra-kv and memra-cli (ci.yml job
#                                        portable-suites and tools/local-ci.sh, memra #545): none
#                                        of the three crates has an artifact-gated test, and the
#                                        wrapper's `verify` over them keeps it that way; a new one
#                                        must be declared here and budgeted there, out loud.
# The static census scans crates/<crate>/src AND crates/<crate>/tests (integration-test binaries;
# libtest prints their paths relative to the binary, so `tests/parity.rs` and `tests/x/mod.rs`
# tests carry no prefix and `tests/x/y.rs` prints `y::`). Extended 2026-09-21 (memra #545 review):
# the src-only scan let a skip born under tests/** go undeclared. The four memra-tokenizer rows
# below are what the extension found: `tests/llama_parity.rs` skips without a GGUF model
# (MEMRA_TEST_MODEL) or a llama-tokenize binary (MEMRA_LLAMA_TOKENIZE). ci.yml runs that crate
# `--lib`, so these never execute there; they are declared so the census is complete in both
# directions and so the run that does execute them (a rig with the artifacts) counts them.
